meters.label: Cents the two systems disagree by

frames.narration: A shopper checks out a cart of 6 lines. The subtotal is 178.08 and the tax is 10%. The cart service holds each price as a float number of dollars.
The Pen line is 21.15, and its tax is exactly 2.115, a tie. In a double the product comes out as 2.1149999999999998, so the cart rounds it down to 2.11.
The cart sends 195.89. The provider works in whole cents, rounds the same tie up to 2.12 and expects 195.90. The two systems disagree by one cent, and nobody changed any data.
Fix 1: store whole minor units and a currency code, 19590 and USD, never a float. The cart now does its arithmetic on integers, which add and compare exactly.
Fix 2: write the rule down once. Round tax on each line, half up, by integer division. Cart, provider and ledger all use it, so a tie rounds the same way everywhere and the gap is gone.
A 100.00 bill is split three ways. Dividing gives 33.33 each and 99.99 in total. Allocation gives the leftover cent to one share: 33.34, 33.33, 33.33, and the parts add up to 10000 cents.
The cart is shown in yen. The yen has exponent 0, so there is no minor unit. The rate is an integer (1492500, 4 decimals) and the subtotal is converted once: 26578, not 26579 from rounding each line.
